notes: Primary contact: Riley Chen (Head of Automation) - very pragmatic, cares about accuracy and platform reliability

Goal: replace rule-based heuristics + macros with ML-driven summarization + auto-tagging. Key KPIs: 95% tag precision on top 12 categories, summary length 2-4 sentences, end-to-end processing <1.2s median for simple emails.
Integration: Zendesk + Freshdesk connectors. They use macros and triggers heavily; need idempotent tag application and dry-run mode.
POC scope: 10k historical tickets for training/labels, live sandbox ingest of new tickets, tag suggestion UI in agent console, server-side macro trigger when confidence >0.9.
Spike & reliability ask: support 10x traffic bursts during release days with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or streaming partial summary). Customer wants documented fallback policy.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market price band but tolerant for predictable reserved capacity. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization to lower token-unit cost.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, audit logs for every inference, KMS key exchange for encryption-at-rest, and option to restrict training on PII. Legal flagged data retention limits for EU customers.
Quote from Riley: "If you can keep agents on-screen and reduce average handle time by 18% without losing tag accuracy, this is a go."
SE notes: try prefix caching for common multi-message threads; evaluate model variants for reranking + tagging ensemble to reduce false positives.
Requested artifacts: example Zendesk trigger JSON, sample macro templates, latency SLO doc, pricing deck with Dedicated capacity options
Current sentiment: optimistic but cautious — procurement needs a clear SLA for burst capacity and a test plan for data residency controls.
